report.headline: STRENGTH trial of Epanova (omega-3 carboxylic acids) stopped early for futility with no cardiovascular benefit demonstrated in statin-treated patients with mixed dyslipidaemia.
report.summary: The STRENGTH trial randomized approximately 13,086 statin-treated patients with hypertriglyceridaemia (TG 175–499 mg/dL) and low HDL-C to Epanova 4 g daily or corn oil placebo, targeting 1,600 primary endpoint events over a planned 3-year median follow-up. The independent data monitoring committee recommended discontinuation because Epanova was unlikely to demonstrate a benefit. No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change was measured in the phase 3 population; phase 2 data showed only a within-arm reduction of −26%. The failure is attributed primarily to design choices — corn oil placebo (which may raise LDL-C and increase control-arm events), a broad MACE composite including softer endpoints (revascularization, unstable angina), and early stopping before the planned event count — and to uncertainty about whether triglyceride lowering via this EPA+DHA formulation is causally linked to cardiovascular risk reduction. Confidence in this assessment is medium.

report.what_would_change_this: Placebo-adjusted triglyceride and apoB changes from a STRENGTH biomarker substudy; a head-to-head comparison of corn oil versus mineral oil placebo effects on LDL-C and MACE in a similar population.
report.readthrough_note: REDUCE-IT demonstrated benefit with pure EPA ethyl ester and mineral oil placebo, suggesting formulation (EPA+DHA vs pure EPA) and placebo choice (corn oil vs mineral oil) critically influence outcomes. Other omega-3 cardiovascular programmes should account for these design and mechanistic differences.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: Open Targets shows no genetic evidence for omega-3-carboxylic acids targets and coronary artery disorder; no verified literature facts with genetic_association before cut-off.
mechanism.notes: No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change available for Epanova 4g/day in phase 2 or phase 3. Phase 2 data (f_055846c61d587f) shows -26% within-arm change at 12 weeks, not placebo-adjusted. Trial stopped early for futility per announcement (f_9a5412963866b9); no hazard ratio or confidence interval reported in available facts. Median follow-up 3 years (f_7d9679918cf6e8). Planned events 1600 (f_6c94b46aa9503b). Corn oil placebo used (f_b7256087b9cbd5).

for.text: Corn oil placebo used as control (f_b7256087b9cbd5), unlike mineral oil in REDUCE-IT; corn oil may raise LDL-C and increase cardiovascular events in the control arm, masking any treatment benefit.

Primary endpoint is a broad MACE composite including coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina (f_06270c902effa7), softer components that dilute treatment effect compared to harder endpoints like CV death/MI/stroke.
Trial stopped early for futility (f_623ee114ace693) before reaching the planned 1600 events (f_6c94b46aa9503b), reducing power to detect a modest benefit.

Inclusion criteria specified TG 175-499 mg/dL (f_e3ff0b15fb7650), a moderate hypertriglyceridemia range; REDUCE-IT enrolled patients with TG ≥150 mg/dL but also required established CVD or diabetes with risk factors, potentially enriching for higher event rates.

against.text: Median follow-up of 3 years (f_7d9679918cf6e8) is reasonable for CV outcome trials; not obviously too short.
Large sample size (~13,086 randomized, f_ff7e7daf43acf6) and event-driven design are standard strengths.

hypotheses.would_settle: Head-to-head comparison of corn oil vs mineral oil placebo effects on LDL-C and MACE in a similar population; or a re-analysis excluding revascularization/unstable angina from the composite.

for.text: Reference table indicates triglycerides causality is 'uncertain' for direct TG lowering, but 'yes' for TG lowering via apoB; the drug's formulation (EPA+DHA carboxylic acids) differs from REDUCE-IT's pure EPA ethyl ester, which may affect apoB and residual risk differently.

No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured in the STRENGTH population (calculator weakest_link: 'triglycerides change not measured'); phase 2 data (f_055846c61d587f) shows -26% within-arm only, not placebo-adjusted.

REDUCE-IT (pure EPA) showed benefit while STRENGTH (EPA+DHA) did not, suggesting the biomarker moved (TG lowering) may not be the causal mediator, or the formulation matters for the causal pathway (e.g., EPA-specific effects on inflammation, platelet function, or apoB).

against.text: Genetic evidence for TG lowering via apoB is causal; if Epanova lowers apoB, a benefit would be expected. No phase 3 apoB data available to test this.
Phase 2 within-arm TG reduction of -26% (f_055846c61d587f) suggests biological activity; absence of placebo-adjusted data prevents quantification, not proof of no effect.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted TG and apoB change from a phase 3 biomarker substudy; Mendelian randomization for EPA+DHA carboxylic acid formulation targets.

for.text: Calculator cannot compute expected HR because no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change is available for the outcome trial dose/population (calculator: 'triglycerides change not measured', outcome: 'not_computable').
Phase 2 biomarker data (f_055846c61d587f, f_bc04df8d50c86f) are within-arm only, not placebo-adjusted; no phase 3 biomarker data in verified facts.
Target genetics listed as 'uncertain' (calculator input) — no human genetic evidence found for omega-3-carboxylic acid targets.

against.text: Verified facts support specific design-or-endpoint and biomarker-not-causal explanations; insufficient_data should be reserved for when no explanation can be supported at all.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted TG and apoB change from STRENGTH biomarker substudy; genetic validation of omega-3-carboxylic acid targets.

for.text: Minimum detectable HR at 80% power is 0.869 (calculator mde_hr_80); if true placebo-adjusted TG lowering is modest, expected benefit could be below this threshold.
Within-arm phase 2 TG reduction -26% (f_055846c61d587f) may overestimate placebo-adjusted effect; true effect could be too small to detect with 1600 events.

against.text: Without placebo-adjusted biomarker change, expected HR cannot be quantified; 'effect too small' cannot be distinguished from 'no effect' or 'wrong biomarker'.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted TG change from phase 3; causal effect estimate per unit TG lowering from genetics.

for.text: Population: statin-treated, high CV risk, hypertriglyceridemia (TG 175-499 mg/dL) and low HDL-C (f_e3ff0b15fb7650, f_d7c3363d2f369e) — similar to REDUCE-IT which showed benefit.

against.text: REDUCE-IT demonstrated benefit in a comparable population (statin-treated, elevated TG, high CV risk), weakening the argument that the population itself precludes benefit.
Corn oil placebo may have increased event rates in control arm, making the population appear less responsive when the issue is comparator choice.

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analysis by baseline TG level, HDL-C, or LDL-C; comparison of event rates in STRENGTH placebo arm vs REDUCE-IT mineral oil arm.

for.text: Corn oil placebo (f_b7256087b9cbd5) may have adverse effects (e.g., raising LDL-C, promoting inflammation) that increase events in control arm, offsetting treatment benefit — this is harm in the comparator, not the drug.

against.text: No safety signal for Epanova itself in verified facts; announcement states 'unlikely to demonstrate benefit' not 'harm'.
Off-target harm typically refers to drug toxicity; here the concern is comparator effects, which falls under design_or_endpoint.

hypotheses.would_settle: LDL-C and inflammatory marker changes in STRENGTH placebo arm vs mineral oil arms in other trials.

for.text: Target genetics listed as 'uncertain' (calculator input) — no human genetic evidence found for omega-3-carboxylic acid targets.

against.text: 'Uncertain' means absence of evidence, not evidence of absence; EPA and DHA have multiple biological targets (GPR120, inflammation, membrane effects) with some genetic support.
REDUCE-IT success with pure EPA suggests at least one omega-3 formulation works; target may be formulation-specific.

hypotheses.would_settle: Mendelian randomization for EPA/DHA carboxylic acid targets; genetic colocalization with CV outcomes.

for.text: Trial stopped early for futility (f_623ee114ace693) by independent data monitoring committee — a scientific decision, not a business decision.

against.text: Large enrollment (~13,086, f_ff7e7daf43acf6) completed; no evidence of poor adherence, recruitment failure, or sponsor-driven termination.

hypotheses.would_settle: Adherence data from STRENGTH; DMC charter and futility boundary details.

issues.issue: Calculator input uses within-arm phase 2 triglyceride change (-26%) that is explicitly not placebo-adjusted (method: 'within-arm_not_placebo_adjusted_phase2'). The automatic check flags this. The calculator correctly returns 'not_computable' with weakest_link 'triglycerides change not measured'. Per protocol, the accepted input before outcome trial results is the placebo-adjusted phase 2 change at the outcome trial dose; since no placebo-adjusted TG change exists for Epanova 4g/day in any source, the changes array should be empty or contain only null entries with missing noted, not a within-arm value that the calculator cannot use.
issues.request: Remove the non-placebo-adjusted TG change from calculator inputs or set pct_change to null with missing: 'no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change available for Epanova 4g/day in phase 2 or 3'.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'biomarker_not_causal' claims 'Reference table lists triglycerides as causal=uncertain' but provides no fact reference (refs array empty). The reference table is not in verified facts; either cite a fact or remove the claim.
issues.request: Search for verified fact containing the biomarker causality reference table (triglycerides causal=uncertain, triglycerides via apoB causal=yes) or remove the unsupported claim.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'design_or_endpoint' states 'corn oil may increase LDL-C and cardiovascular events, biasing toward null' and references REDUCE-IT's mineral oil, but cited fact f_b7256087b9cbd5 only says 'corn oil control' with no mention of LDL-C effects or REDUCE-IT. The comparison to REDUCE-IT is not supported by verified facts.
issues.request: Find verified facts about corn oil placebo effects on LDL-C/events in STRENGTH or REDUCE-IT's mineral oil placebo, or qualify the claim as speculative.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'target_not_causal' cites 'calculator' as reference for target_genetics='uncertain', but references must be to verified facts (f_* IDs). The calculator input is not a verified fact.
issues.request: Either find a verified fact about target genetics for omega-3-carboxylic acids, or change refs to empty and note the source is calculator input assumption.

issues.issue: Multiple inclusion threshold values for triglycerides in verified facts: 180 mg/dL (f_01b774dba5a165), 100 mg/dL (f_b43d35fe805760 - actually LDL-C), 175-499 mg/dL (f_e3ff0b15fb7650 from announcement). The calculator uses baseline 175 mg/dL. The case should clarify which threshold reflects the final protocol.
issues.request: Confirm final inclusion TG threshold from announcement (175-499 mg/dL) and note discrepancy with earlier protocol (180 mg/dL).

issues.issue: n_randomized discrepancies: 13,078 (CTgov f_24faaecc143f62), 13,086 (pmid:30125052 f_f8fa2acefb0923), 13,086 (announcement f_ff7e7daf43acf6). Minor but should be noted.
issues.request: Note the discrepancy and use announcement value (13,086) as most recent.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'effect_too_small' speculates 'If true placebo-adjusted TG reduction is modest (<20%), expected HR may exceed MDE HR of 0.869' but no placebo-adjusted data exists to support any quantification. Status 'undetermined' is correct but the 'for' argument is purely hypothetical.
issues.request: Qualify that this is purely speculative without placebo-adjusted biomarker data.

issues.issue: The 'biomarker_not_causal' hypothesis claims 'Reference table indicates triglycerides causality is uncertain for direct TG lowering, but yes for TG lowering via apoB' but provides no fact citation for this reference table. This is a key causal claim without support in the verified facts.
issues.request: Either add a verified fact for the biomarker causality reference table, or remove/qualify the unsupported claim in the hypothesis.

issues.issue: The 'design_or_endpoint' hypothesis claims corn oil placebo 'may raise LDL-C and increase cardiovascular events in the control arm' but cites only f_b7256087b9cbd5 which states 'corn oil control' - it does not support the mechanistic claim about LDL-C raising or event increase.
issues.request: Either find a verified fact showing corn oil raises LDL-C/increases events in this trial, or rephrase the hypothesis to state this as a concern/hypothesis rather than a supported fact.

issues.issue: Multiple hypotheses (design_or_endpoint, biomarker_not_causal, population, off_target_harm) reference REDUCE-IT trial results (pure EPA benefit, mineral oil placebo) but no REDUCE-IT facts are in the verified facts. These are external knowledge not part of the evidence base for this case.
issues.request: Either add verified facts for REDUCE-IT results, or remove/rephrase comparisons to REDUCE-IT as speculative rather than evidence-supported.

issues.issue: The calculator input for changes has an empty source string. While method correctly states 'no_placebo_adjusted_data_available', the source should reference the phase 2 facts that were evaluated (f_055846c61d587f) and note they are not placebo-adjusted.
issues.request: Update calculator input changes[0].source to reference f_055846c61d587f with note that it is within-arm phase 2 data, not placebo-adjusted.

issues.issue: Inclusion threshold has multiple values in verified facts (180 mg/dL f_01b774dba5a165, 175-499 mg/dL f_e3ff0b15fb7650, complex criteria f_d7c3363d2f369e). The hypothesis uses 175-499 from announcement but does not acknowledge the discrepancy.
issues.request: Clarify in hypothesis which threshold is the final protocol version and note the discrepancy in verified facts.

issues.issue: The 'insufficient_data' hypothesis's 'against' argument is a meta-argument about categorization rules ('insufficient_data should be reserved for when no explanation can be supported at all') rather than evidence from verified facts.
issues.request: Replace meta-argument with evidence-based counterpoints from verified facts, or remove if no such evidence exists.
